title: A nonconstant map between point-exceptional fibres is an ambient isomorphism nearby
statement: Let $T,S$ be integral regular Noetherian schemes of dimension $2$, with Noetherian meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $t\in T$ and $s\in S$ be closed points, with $\dim\mathcal O_{S,s}=2$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $a:T'=\operatorname{Bl}_tT\to T$ and $b:S'=\operatorname{Bl}_sS\to S$ be the blowups of the reduced closed points [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Write $E=a^{-1}(t)$ and $F=b^{-1}(s)$ for their scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre], with closed immersions $i_E:E\to T'$ and $i_F:F\to S'$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $h:T'\to S'$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and birational, meaning that it restricts to an isomorphism between dense open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. Suppose there is a morphism $v:E\to F$ such that $h\circ i_E=i_F\circ v$ and the topological image $v(E)$ contains more than one point. Then there is an open subscheme $N\subseteq S'$ containing $F$ such that $h^{-1}(N)\to N$ is an isomorphism. Moreover, $v$ is an isomorphism and $h^{-1}(|F|)=|E|$ as underlying closed subsets of $T'$.

source.place: Tag 0C5R (resolve-lemma-proper-birational-regular-surfaces), proof from the paragraph beginning Let E be the exceptional fibre through the conormal, unramifiedness and isomorphism-neighbourhood argument. The source centre may have local dimension one, in which case the nonconstant-image hypothesis is impossible.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-point-blowup-exceptional-conormal] to $t\in T$. Its local dimension is either $1$ or $2$. In dimension $1$, $E$ is a one-point scheme, contradicting the hypothesis on $v(E)$. Thus it is $2$. Apply the same node to $s\in S$, whose local dimension is $2$ by hypothesis. Consequently $E$ and $F$ are integral regular proper projective lines over $\kappa(t)$ and $\kappa(s)$, respectively, and their conormal bundles are their positive twists. Both are effective Cartier divisors. By [lem-sfb-regular-point-blowup-geometry], both ambient blowups $T'$ and $S'$ are integral regular Noetherian. By [rem-pc-regular-normal], their local rings and those of the regular curve $F$ are normal. No excellence, algebraic closedness or equality of residue fields has been used.

source.place: Tag 0C5R (resolve-lemma-proper-birational-regular-surfaces), exceptional-fibre and conormal argument, lines 4929-4964.

proof.text: The composite $E\hookrightarrow T'\xrightarrow{h}S'$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Since $F\hookrightarrow S'$ is separated, [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] applied over $S'$ shows that $v:E\to F$ is proper. Its image is therefore closed. It is irreducible, since $E$ is integral, and contains more than one point. A proper irreducible closed subset of an integral one-dimensional scheme is a single closed point: otherwise its chain through its own generic point and that of the whole curve has length at least two. Thus $v$ is surjective and dominant. Let $\eta_F$ be the generic point of $F$. By [lem-sbc-regular-cartier-generic-stalk-dvr], $\mathcal O_{S',\eta_F}$ is a DVR. Its only primes are zero and its maximal ideal (every nonzero prime in a local PID is maximal), so it has dimension one. The birationality required by [lem-sfb-normal-modification-codimension-one] holds: $T'$ and $S'$ are integral, so the given dense opens on which $h$ is an isomorphism contain their unique generic points, $h$ maps the generic point of $T'$ to that of $S'$, and the isomorphism of opens induces an isomorphism of the local rings there. Apply clause (2) of [lem-sfb-normal-modification-codimension-one] to the proper birational $h$, with integral, hence reduced, source, and Noetherian target $S'$ (step 1). We obtain an open $U\subseteq S'$ containing $\eta_F$ over which $h$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C5R (resolve-lemma-proper-birational-regular-surfaces), exceptional-fibre and conormal argument, lines 4929-4964.

proof.text: Under $h^{-1}(U)\cong U$, the closed subscheme $E\cap h^{-1}(U)$ becomes a closed subscheme of $F\cap U$, because $h i_E=i_F v$. It is nonempty and contains the generic point of $F\cap U$: $v$ is surjective and $\eta_F\in U$. A closed subscheme of an integral scheme containing its generic point has zero defining ideal (on an affine domain its ideal injects into the fraction field). Hence this closed subscheme equals $F\cap U$. In particular $v$ is an isomorphism on these dense opens and induces an isomorphism of function fields. Set $k=\kappa(s)$ and equip $E$ with its $k$-structure through $v$. The scheme $F$ is proper over $k$ by step 1; since $v$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] gives that $E$ is proper over $k$ as well. Properness implies separatedness and finite type, so $E,F$ are integral separated finite-type $k$-schemes of dimension one. The map $v$ is a proper dominant $k$-morphism, birational by the dense-open calculation, and $F$ has normal local rings. All hypotheses of [lem-trf-proper-birational-normal-curve-iso] hold; it gives that $v$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C5R (resolve-lemma-proper-birational-regular-surfaces), exceptional-fibre and conormal argument, lines 4929-4964.

proof.text: Form the canonical map $c:v^*\mathcal C_{F/S'}\to\mathcal C_{E/T'}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-functorial]. At the generic point of $E$, it is an isomorphism: on the open $U$ of step 2 the ambient map is an isomorphism and step 3 identifies the two closed subschemes. The affine formula for $c$ is the induced map on ideals modulo their squares, so those identifications identify $c$ with the isomorphism of conormal modules. In particular it is nonzero there. By [lem-sfb-point-blowup-exceptional-conormal], choose identifications of $E,F$ with projective lines carrying their conormal bundles to $\mathcal O(1)$. Under these choices $v$ becomes an absolute isomorphism between the two projective lines and $c$ becomes a map from the pullback of the target positive twist to the source positive twist. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-line-twist-rigidity] to conclude that $c$ is an isomorphism everywhere on $E$. Its formulation permits the two originally different residue fields.

source.place: Tag 0C5R (resolve-lemma-proper-birational-regular-surfaces), exceptional-fibre and conormal argument, lines 4929-4964.

proof.text: Use $v$ to identify $E$ with $F$. Then $i_E:E\hookrightarrow T'$ and $j=i_F\circ v:E\hookrightarrow S'$ are closed immersions with $h i_E=j$. The ideal defining $j$ is the ideal of $F$, with its conormal sheaf pulled back by $v$; on affine opens both are the same ideal modulo its square under the isomorphism $v$. Thus the conormal morphism for these two immersions is exactly the map $c$ in step 4. It is surjective because it is invertible. Properness of $h$ implies local finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-conormal-surjection-unramified] to these two immersions and $h$. For each $e\in E$ it supplies an open neighbourhood $W_e\subseteq T'$ on which $h|_{W_e}$ is unramified.

source.place: Tag 0C5R (resolve-lemma-proper-birational-regular-surfaces), exceptional-fibre and conormal argument, lines 4929-4964.

proof.text: For each $e\in E$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points] to $h|_{W_e}$. It is quasi-finite at $e$, hence so is $h$: the same affine neighbourhoods in $W_e$ are affine open neighbourhoods in $T'$, as in [pqf-def-quasifinite]. For any $y\in F$, choose $e=v^{-1}(y)$ by step 3. The local ring $\mathcal O_{S',y}$ is normal by step 1, and $h$ is quasi-finite at $e$ over $y$. Clause (4) of [lem-sfb-normal-modification-codimension-one] therefore puts $y$ in the maximal open isomorphism locus $N$ of $h$. Consequently $F\subseteq N$ and $h^{-1}(N)\to N$ is an isomorphism, as required.

source.place: Tag 0C5R (resolve-lemma-proper-birational-regular-surfaces), exceptional-fibre and conormal argument, lines 4929-4964.

proof.text: We already proved that $v$ is an isomorphism in step 3. Since $|F|\subseteq N$, every point in $h^{-1}(|F|)$ lies in $h^{-1}(N)$. The isomorphism $h^{-1}(N)\to N$ gives precisely one preimage of each point of $F$, and the inclusion $E\hookrightarrow T'$ with $v:E\cong F$ supplies such a preimage. Thus every point of $h^{-1}(|F|)$ is in $|E|$. The reverse inclusion is the equality $h i_E=i_F v$. Therefore $h^{-1}(|F|)=|E|$.

Steps 1-7 follow 0C5R:
- 1: the d=1 source centre is excluded by #v(E)>1.
- 2: v proper via proper-to-separated-target; surjective by the dimension-1 chain argument; DVR at eta_F; clause (2) of the normal-modification node.
- 3: the closed subscheme containing the generic point has zero ideal; all common-field hypotheses of the curve-iso theorem are checked.
- 4: c is a generic isomorphism by the affine formula; twist rigidity applies.
- 5: the conormal map for (i_E, i_F v) is c, which is surjective, so h is unramified near E.
- 6: quasi-finite on W_e, then clause (4) gives F inside N.
- 7: elementary.

New nodes, all true and statement-only:
- point-blowup-exceptional-conormal: global 0AGQ plus the d=1 case. The local-surface, per-surface and regular-flag blowup nodes lack the conormal identification, so it is not a duplicate.
- projective-line-twist-rigidity: Pic=Z and ampleness preserved by an absolute isomorphism, Gamma(O)=k.
- conormal-surjection-unramified: 067L plus 02GF plus Nakayama. Tested on a closed immersion and on x->x^n.

The item is not superseded: it is still unsplit in live and side-live, with statement and stmt_deps unchanged. The parent's step 4 matches the conclusion.
